AfterPowerAmountChanged.rationale: SPLIT ACROSS TWO SIM HOOKS, and the split is correct -- this is the one unit in half A where the sim's re-architecture of a single C# hook is exactly right rather than approximately right. Hook.AfterPowerAmountChanged fires from BOTH of PowerCmd's pipelines: step 23 of audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json (PowerCmd.cs:153-157, a brand-new power, gated on modifiedAmount != 0) and step 33 (PowerCmd.cs:243-246, a re-stack, gated on (int)modifiedOffset != 0). The sim has a separate hook for each -- on_power_applied at cmds.py:327 for the new-power branch and on_power_amount_changed at cmds.py:312 for the stacking branch -- and this power implements BOTH and routes them to one _maybe_draw. So a first Bash and a second Bash both draw, on both sides. All three C# guards are present: amount <= 0 (ViciousPower.cs:21 vs powers.py:1167, where the sim's delta is `existing.amount - old_amount` at cmds.py:313 and so is 0 for a Single-stack no-op -- correctly not a draw), applier == base.Owner (:21 vs :1167), and power is VulnerablePower (:21 vs :1167's name != 'vulnerable'). Note C# has NO target-side test, and neither does the sim: Vicious draws whenever its owner applies Vulnerable to anyone. Both sides also miss the Artifact case identically -- a fully blocked Vulnerable returns at cmds.py:306 before any notification, matching C#'s != 0 gates.

This power is the reason a missing applier= matters, and it is worth recording where it is safe. Vicious keys entirely on `applier is self.owner`, so any sim site that applies Vulnerable WITHOUT applier= is silently invisible to it. Checked the ported Vulnerable appliers: the Ironclad card Bash and its siblings pass applier=ctx.player, and monster applications pass applier=self, so no ported Vulnerable source is applier-less. Named trigger: adding a Vulnerable application that omits applier=, which would make Vicious silently stop working -- the same class of latent break as audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's note N2.
Neither side ticks or removes it; it draws for the rest of the combat. Both agree.
